steps.title: Prepare syringe plug A
steps.instruction: Construct the syringe plug that provides separate medium (A1) and air (A2) entries for a 50 mL syringe.

substeps.instruction: Push two 12 cm glass tubes (Ø 6 mm) through a rubber plug (Ø 6 mm) so that ~2 cm of each glass tube protrudes from the plug.
Autoclave two 10 cm PVC tubes (Ø 6 mm) to increase flexibility, then slide each PVC tube over the external portion of a glass tube until it reaches the rubber plug.
Attach a 0.2 µm Acrodisc CR syringe filter to the end of one PVC tube.
Attach a tube connector CT45.1 (Ø 1.6–4.8 mm) to the end of the other PVC tube.
Insert the assembled rubber plug with glass and PVC tubes into the syringe barrel and close the syringe; this assembly is the syringe plug (A).
Screw the Luer‑Lock syringe adapter CT62.1 (Ø 1.6 mm) onto the syringe tip.
Connect a piece of silicone tubing (Ø 0.5 mm, length sufficient to reach the chemostat inflow) to the adapter and secure with a tube holder/clamp.
Cut a silicone tube (Ø 0.5 mm) to the distance between the syringe and the peristaltic pump.
Join this silicone tube to the CT45.1 connector on the PVC tube designated for medium (A1).
Fit a CT33.1 connector (Ø 1.6 mm) onto the opposite end of the silicone tube.
Attach three 24 cm pieces of PharMed BPT tubing (Ø 5 mm inner, Ø 1.6 mm wall) to the CT33.1 connector; these will run through the peristaltic pump.
Place a fourth CT33.1 connector on the pump‑exit end of the three BPT pieces and connect a second silicone tube (Ø 0.5 mm, length to reach the medium bottle).

steps.title: Assemble chemostat vessel B
steps.instruction: Build the 500 mL chemostat bottle with inflow, outflow, and sampling connections.

substeps.instruction: Place a stirring bar into the 500 mL clear glass bottle.
Prepare a 8 cm glass outflow tube (Ø 6 mm) that will sit inside the screw‑cap hole (Ø 4 cm) to define the chemostat volume.
Combine the screw‑cap (Ø 4 cm) with a lid that has three holes (two Ø 0.4 mm, one Ø 0.5 mm) to form the chemostat cap (B).
Cut two silicone tubes: ~20 cm for inflow (B1) and ~25 cm for outflow (B2).
Thread both tubes through the two Ø 0.4 mm holes of the lid.
For inflow (B1): attach a CT45.1 connector (Ø 1.6–4.8 mm) with the connector facing inward; join the other end to the silicone tube coming from the syringe (step 1) via a CT33.1 connector.

For outflow (B2): pass the ~25 cm silicone tube through the 8 cm glass outflow tube, secure the glass tube with a CT33.1 connector, and attach a CT45.1 connector to the external silicone end (to later connect to the waste bottle).
Close the bottle with the assembled cap (B).

Prepare the sampling needle (B3): cut the tip off a 1‑10 µL pipette tip, insert it into the Ø 0.5 mm hole of the lid, then push the neoLab Luer‑Lock cannula through the tip to hold the needle in place.
Add a CT33.1 connector to each end of the inflow and outflow silicone tubes.
Seal all three lid holes with silicone, ensuring the seal is airtight, and let cure for 24 h.

steps.title: Construct medium bottle C
steps.instruction: Prepare the 5 L (or sized) medium reservoir with its inlet cap.

substeps.instruction: Cut a silicone tube (Ø 0.5 mm) ~35 cm long (≈25 cm to bottom + 10 cm extra).
Thread this tube through one Ø 0.4 mm hole of a three‑hole lid.
Attach a CT45.1 connector (Ø 1.6–4.8 mm) to the tube end that will sit inside the bottle.
Attach a CT33.1 connector (Ø 1.6 mm) to the external end of the tube; this tube (C1) will later mate with the syringe‑plug medium connector (A1).
Cut a ~4 cm silicone piece and knot it on both sides of the second Ø 0.4 mm hole to block it (or use a two‑hole lid).
Fit the three‑hole lid onto the 5 L bottle and secure.
Place an Acrodisc CR syringe filter onto the Ø 0.5 mm hole of the lid, positioning the slip‑outlet side outward.
Seal the entire assembly with silicone, avoiding coverage of the filter, and allow to cure.

steps.title: Construct waste bottle D
steps.instruction: Prepare the 5 L waste reservoir with its outlet cap.

substeps.instruction: Cut a silicone tube (Ø 0.5 mm) ~14 cm long.
Thread this tube through one Ø 0.4 mm hole of a three‑hole lid.
Attach a CT45.1 connector (Ø 1.6–4.8 mm) to the tube end that will be inside the bottle.
Attach a CT33.1 connector (Ø 1.6 mm) to the external end of the tube; this tube (D1) will later connect to the ~25 cm silicone outflow tube from the chemostat (B2).
Cut a ~4 cm silicone piece and knot it on both sides of the remaining Ø 0.4 mm hole (or use a two‑hole lid).
Fit the three‑hole lid onto the waste bottle and secure.
Place an Acrodisc CR syringe filter onto the Ø 0.5 mm hole of the lid, slip‑outlet side outward.
Seal the whole assembly with silicone, keeping the filter uncovered, and let cure.

steps.title: Autoclave assembled components
steps.instruction: Sterilize all assembled parts (syringe plug, chemostat caps, medium and waste bottle caps, tubing connections) in an autoclave before installation.

steps.title: Install chemostats on stir plates
steps.instruction: Place each 500 mL chemostat bottle on a magnetic stir plate, set a gentle stirring speed to maintain homogeneity, and position the assembled cap (B) securely.

steps.title: Create over‑pressure system
steps.instruction: Mount the syringe on a tripod behind the chemostats, connect its air‑inlet PVC tube (A2) through the Acrodisc filter on the syringe plug, and link to an aquarium‑type air pump.

substeps.instruction: Adjust the air pump pressure so the syringe plug is pressurised but does not pop off.
Secure all tubing with cable ties where needed.

steps.title: Complete fluid circuit A‑B‑C‑D
steps.instruction: Connect the medium, chemostat, and waste lines to close the loop from the medium bottle (C) through the syringe plug (A), chemostat vessel (B), and waste bottle (D).

substeps.instruction: Join the medium‑inlet silicone tube from the medium cap (C1) to the CT45.1 connector of the syringe‑plug medium entry (A1).
Link the syringe‑plug air exit (A2) to the air pump as described above.
Connect the chemostat outflow silicone tube (B2) to the CT45.1 connector of the waste‑bottle inlet (D1).
Verify that all CT33.1 and CT45.1 connectors are tight.

steps.title: Prime system and verify flow
steps.instruction: Run the peristaltic pump to fill the chemostats with medium and confirm proper inflow and outflow.

substeps.instruction: Start pump (25) and allow medium to circulate for at least 24 h.
Check that the chemostat volume is completely replaced within this period.
Adjust pump speed or tube diameter to achieve the desired dilution rate (e.g., d = 0.5 day⁻¹ for 400 mL volume with 200 mL day⁻¹ renewal, using a 0.8 mm pump tube).

steps.title: Sample chemostat culture
steps.instruction: Perform sterile sampling while maintaining system over‑pressure.

substeps.instruction: Turn off the air inflow to prevent bubbling.
Wipe the sampling needle with 70 % ethanol and flame the exposed tip with a lab torch.
Insert the sterile needle to the same depth as before.
Open the needle cap and withdraw the desired volume with a syringe.
Withdraw the needle, re‑wipe with 70 % ethanol, and flame the tip again.
Restart the air inflow.

steps.title: Set dilution rate for experiment
steps.instruction: Calculate and program the pump to achieve the target dilution rate based on chemostat volume and desired daily medium turnover.

substeps.instruction: Determine chemostat volume (e.g., 400 mL).
Choose desired dilution rate (e.g., d = 0.5 day⁻¹ → 200 mL day⁻¹).
Select pump tubing diameter (e.g., 0.8 mm) and set pump speed according to manufacturer’s flow‑rate chart to deliver the calculated volume per day.
Confirm that the dilution rate does not exceed the organism’s growth rate to avoid wash‑out.
